summary: Session tenant prefix truncation blocks internal reports access
description:
Issue summary: Several internal users cannot access the Internal Reports app after SSO login. The auth flow completes, but the reports service returns 403 + 'missing_tenant_claim'. This appears tied to tenant prefix information being truncated during session merge between regional sessions.

Users affected: ~7 users in last 4 hours, all with long org prefixes ( > 48 characters ) in their Okta org attribute. Occurrence: Intermittent but reproducible for affected users whenever their session is merged from eu-west to us-east or when they switch consoles across regions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use an account whose Okta 'org' attribute has a long prefix name (> 48 chars).
2) Sign in via SSO to the Console in eu-west, then switch to us-east via the region switcher (or have an existing session merge).
5) Check auth-proxy logs for header 'x-tenant' value length and for any truncation warnings.
observed_logs: 2026-03-10T15:12:02Z auth-proxy[proxy-3] WARN header_truncate: 'x-tenant' length 128 > 64, truncating to 64 (req_id=abc123)
2026-03-10T15:12:02Z internal-reports svc ERROR auth: tenant claim mismatch: expected 'redwood-enterprise-longprefix-abcdef', got 'redwood-enterprise-longprefix-abcdef' (truncated)
2026-03-10T15:12:03Z okta-session[sessionmgr] INFO session_merge: merged session eu-west->us-east for user u123 (session_id=sess-9f7)
investigation_notes: 15:30 — Reproduced locally with a test account having org prefix length 72. Confirmed truncation in auth-proxy logs.

16:00 — Hypothesis: Recent Envoy header buffer/size filter (rolled out in prod-us-east on 2026-03-09 via infra PR #4521: commit 9b7a2c) enforces 64-char header limits and truncates tenant headers when sessions migrate across regions.

16:45 — Auth team looked at codepath: tenant is passed in 'x-tenant' header from console proxy -> internal-reports. No fallback to token claim if header missing. Role resolution expects full prefix. Truncation causes RBAC lookup to fail and returns 403.
17:20 — Correlated incidents: linked to INT-462199 (cookie-stripping proxy redirect loop) — both involve recent proxy changes but different subsystems.
comments: 2026-03-10 18:02 — Diego Alvarez: Assigned to auth-proxy oncall. I can confirm header truncation in staging after replay. Blocking fix: revert header-size filter or widen limit.
2026-03-10 18:45 — SRE (Amina R.): Short-term workaround: adding header fallback that reads tenant from session token claim when 'x-tenant' appears truncated. Patching canary in prod-us-east now.
2026-03-11 09:12 — Maya Chen: Customer-facing note: internal reports team notified; PagerDuty reroutes created. Asked for ETA on full fix and rollback plan.

2026-03-12 11:00 — Diego Alvarez: Canary patch rolled out to 3 hosts. Monitoring for 2 hours showed successful logins for truncated accounts. Planning full rollback of Envoy filter in next deploy window if no regression is observed.

2026-03-13 08:30 — Auth team (J. Patel): Confirmed root cause: Envoy header_rewrite filter introduced in infra PR trimmed headers >64 chars. Follow-up PR to increase limit and add token-claim fallback submitted: https://github.com/redwood/auth-proxy/pull/4602 (review pending).
resolution: Workaround: Added server-side tolerance in internal-reports to consult session token tenant claim when x-tenant header mismatch detected. Canary verification successful. Long-term fix: revert restrictive Envoy header limit and merge auth-proxy PR #4602 to increase header length and implement robust fallback. Rollout plan: staged deploy starting 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC with monitoring and automatic rollback on increased 5xx rate.
next_steps: 1) Complete code review and merge PR #4602 (auth-proxy) to remove truncation behavior and add token-claim fallback.
2) Schedule staged deploy to prod-us-east during maintenance window 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC.
3) Post-deploy: run targeted verification with 10 test accounts with varied tenant prefix lengths and cross-region session merges.
4) Update runbook to include tenant header size checks and add automated alert for header_truncate WARN messages.
5) Communicate resolution to impacted teams and close ticket after 48h of clean metrics.
